summary: Canadian psychologist Jordan Peterson rose from a Toronto professorship to fame in 2016 by opposing trans rights law Bill C-16, spreading mystical, hierarchy-worshipping ideas that feed the far right, before a benzodiazepine addiction derailed him.

evidence.note: Born June 1962 in Edmonton, raised in Fairview, Alberta
Long segment on fascist mysticism and his influences Jung, Eliade, Campbell
Moves to Boston to teach at Harvard, later returns to Toronto
Self Authoring Suite sold as an online self-help program
2016 campaign against Bill C-16 and trans pronouns launches his fame
Response to 2018 incel van attack: enforced monogamy, women as chaos
Misleading claim of tribal membership used to deflect racism charges
12 Rules for Life (2018) aimed at insecure men
Benzodiazepine dependence after wife's 2019 cancer diagnosis, rehab
Daughter takes him to Russia for an induced-coma detox
2020 Serbia trip and COVID; still not recovered at release

notes: Primary theme is a judgment call between fascism-far-right (the hosts' stated framing: his ideas feed fascism) and misogyny-manosphere. main_span runs from the 2016 C-16 fame to his 2020 collapse; he was alive but inactive at release, so end is 2020, not null. Judeo-Bolshevism and Weimar material is background, not covered. Serbia is brief and left out of setting.
